head: 250884688bc0cb776467606356da37d8e45b73e3
summary: AC5.1 and B1 are met and tested at unit and real Kafka/PostgreSQL level. One major finding: the amount rule ignores the command's currency and the 'single-currency' justification is not backed by spec or ADR; a non-EUR amount is compared with a EUR-minor-unit limit.

acceptance_criteria.evidence: AmountRuleTest boundaries 100000/100001; AssessRiskIT reply types over real Kafka
AssessRiskService writes inbox and outbox reply in one @Transactional; redelivery test asserts exactly one reply

findings.description: Javadoc claims the platform is single-currency (EUR) so one threshold serves every payment, but neither docs/spec.md nor ADR 0014 says so. AssessRiskCommand carries currency and AssessRiskService drops it, so a payment in another currency is compared with a minor-unit limit meant for EUR (ADR 0004: no arithmetic/comparison across currencies). No test covers a non-EUR command.
findings.suggestion: Pass the currency to the rule and reject/raise on a currency different from the configured one (or record single-currency as a decision in ADR 0014), and add a named test.

findings.description: A non-positive amount makes the use case throw InvalidAssessmentException after the inbox insert; rollback, retry and DLT behaviour for it is untested, and the redelivery test only covers an approved case.
